title: Árpád dynasty
fact_summary: The family that ruled the Hungarians from the conquest to the early 14th century. The name is modern; the oldest Hungarian history says the dukes were to come from the line of Álmos.

claims.text: A 2021 genetic study, in its historical summary, says that from the time of the conquest “to the early fourteenth century” the Hungarians “were ruled by descendants of the Arpad family”.
claims.certainty_reason: The study's summary of the background, not its own finding; the works it cites have not been opened.

claims.text: The same study notes that the term Árpád Dynasty “was initiated in the eighteenth century for the first royal house of Hungary”, when scholars named it after Álmos's son Árpád.
claims.certainty_reason: The study's summary of the background, not its own finding; the works it cites have not been opened.

claims.text: The Gesta Hungarorum, written about 1200, has the seven leaders swear that “they and their descendants would always have a duke from the line of Duke Álmos”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says, read in Martyn Rady's English translation in the open copy linked under Sources. The Latin has not been compared.

claims.text: The same work says Álmos, father of Árpád, descended from the line of King Attila.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says, read in Martyn Rady's English translation in the open copy linked under Sources. The Latin has not been compared.

claims.text: A 2020 study found that King Béla III and one other skeleton from the royal basilica share a paternal lineage, which it named R-ARP.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The paternal lineage “provides a direct link between Bela III and his ancestor Árpád”, “if there was no hidden paternity” along the line.
claims.certainty_reason: Rests on the written genealogy being right at every generation, as the authors themselves say. No earlier member of the family has been sequenced.

open_questions.text: The oath in the Gesta was written down three hundred years after the events it describes. Is it a memory, or a later justification of the dynasty's right to rule?
Which written sources give the genealogy between Árpád and Stephen? None has been read yet.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
